gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu stands towering tall, its terminals held well away from the stroke bodies, under a Nippo heading cut like wire. Wiry and sharp against tall and loose, they never blur.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Technical and wiry, Nippo is a rope-thin outline. Noto Sans Ogham sits below with wide gaps in the e and tall bodies, so a long passage reads bold and generously open.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-hungarian: Nippo draws every letter as if with one nib, small letters standing nearly as tall as capitals. Noto Sans Old Hungarian, a plain sans, keeps its apertures open at tiny sizes, so the text stays legible below.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Thin wire up top, dense sans-serif below. Nippo holds one stroke thickness throughout every letter, and Noto Sans Old Italic keeps curve endings apart, so body text can sit fairly small beneath a heading.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-north-arab: Nippo's letters look cut from wire, with no brush-style swell anywhere, and the small letters stand almost capital-sized. And Noto Sans Old North Arabian, a plain sans, packs a dense tall lowercase band whose terminals point outward like tongs.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Nippo's pen pressure never wavers from first letter to last, and its small letters stand nearly as tall as capitals, cut like wire. Noto Sans Old Permic is a plain sans whose rounded forms stay open to the side, so a long stretch reads smoothly.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Nippo looks drawn with a single nib, its small letters standing proud and almost capital-sized like cut wire. Noto Sans Old Persian, a plain sans, lets lofty tall lowercase and open counters breathe into the white space.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Clean and technical, Nippo has no thick and thin parts in any letter, only cut-wire lines. Noto Sans Old Sogdian is a sans-serif with a tall x-height and wide mouths, so a long passage stays crisp.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Approachable meets technical here: Nippo runs a single flat line weight through every glyph, wire-like and sharp. Noto Sans Old Turkic, a plain sans, does the opposite job, with chunky tall lowercase and open-mouthed curves that stay clear.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Noto Sans Oriya keeps its curves generously open and its small letters nearly as tall as capitals, below a Nippo heading. That heading looks laser-cut from one sheet, a single cutting width throughout.
